If a body of mass $10\text{ kg}$ is placed on the surface of the Earth, then the pull of the Earth on the body will be
(Note: The value of acceleration due to gravity is $9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.)
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The pull of Earth on a body is its weight $W = mg = 10\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m/s}^2 = 98\text{ N}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Two forces ($9\text{ N}$ and $12\text{ N}$) act at the right angle at point O, as shown in the given figure. What will be the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Magnitude $R = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ N}$. By vector addition (head-to-tail / parallelogram law), the resultant lies along OQ.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
If a body obeys the first condition of equilibrium, then which of the following options will equate to zero?

• I. Linear acceleration
• II. Vector sum of all the forces
• III. Vector sum of all the torques
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: According to the first condition of equilibrium, the vector sum of all external forces acting on a body is zero ($\sum \vec{F} = 0$, statement II). By Newton's second law ($\sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}$), zero net force also implies zero linear acceleration ($\vec{a} = 0$, statement I). Statement III ($\sum \vec{\tau} = 0$) is the second condition of equilibrium.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If a force of $4\text{ N}$ is applied by a student on a door handle and the moment of force is $16\text{ Nm}$, then the distance of the pivot from the point of applied force is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: From $\tau = F \times d$, the moment arm (perpendicular distance from the pivot) is $d = \frac{\tau}{F} = \frac{16\text{ Nm}}{4\text{ N}} = 4\text{ m}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
In the given diagram, two weights '$W_1$' and '$W_2$' are placed on a rod whereas ($W_1 > W_2$). For keeping the rod in the equilibrium position, then

• I. increase '$W_2$' and decrease '$x$'
• II. increase '$W_2$' and '$x$' remain same
• III. increase '$x$' and '$W_2$' remain the same
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: By the principle of moments, balancing the larger anticlockwise weight $W_1$ at distance $y$ requires increasing the clockwise moment $W_2 \times x$. In the given diagram, the pivot is shifted towards $W_1$ so the moment arm $x$ of the lighter weight $W_2$ is increased while $W_2$ remains the same (statement III only).

crqs.question: Describe the THREE states of equilibrium on the basis of the centre of gravity and give one daily-life example of each.
crqs.answer: 1. Stable equilibrium: CoG rises on slight displacement and body returns to original position (e.g., book lying flat on a table). 2. Unstable equilibrium: CoG lowers on displacement and body topples (e.g., pencil balanced on its tip). 3. Neutral equilibrium: CoG height remains unchanged on displacement (e.g., rolling ball on a horizontal floor).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.2 & Model Paper II Q.2

crqs.question:
A hanging picture frame is in a state of static equilibrium. The picture frame has a mass of $0.3\text{ kg}$ and is suspended from a single point by a thin wire.

If a small object of $0.1\text{ kg}$ is hung at any one corner from the bottom of the picture frame, then explain how the addition of the small object affects the balance of these forces and the stability of the picture frame.
crqs.question_text:
A hanging picture frame is in a state of static equilibrium. The picture frame has a mass of $0.3\text{ kg}$ and is suspended from a single point by a thin wire.

If a small object of $0.1\text{ kg}$ is hung at any one corner from the bottom of the picture frame, then explain how the addition of the small object affects the balance of these forces and the stability of the picture frame.

rubric.description: 1 mark for explaining that hanging the 0.1 kg mass at one corner creates an unbalanced torque (moment) and disturbs the static equilibrium.
1 mark for stating that the centre of gravity (CoG) of the picture frame shifts towards the weighted corner.
1 mark for explaining that the frame tilts towards the weighted corner until the new centre of gravity aligns vertically below the suspension point, reducing its initial balanced stability.

crqs.answer:
1. **Disturbance of Equilibrium (Unbalanced Torque):** Initially, the picture frame is in static equilibrium because its centre of gravity lies vertically below the single suspension point. Hanging a $0.1\text{ kg}$ object at one bottom corner introduces an additional downward weight ($W = mg = 1\text{ N}$) at a distance from the line of action of tension, creating an unbalanced torque.
2. **Shift in Centre of Gravity:** The combined centre of gravity of the frame-and-mass system shifts away from the geometric centre towards the corner where the $0.1\text{ kg}$ mass is attached.
3. **Effect on Position and Stability:** Due to the unbalanced moment and shifted centre of gravity, the picture frame tilts downwards on the weighted side until the new centre of gravity comes to rest vertically below the point of suspension.

erqs.question: State the principle of moments and explain the two conditions required for a rigid body to remain in complete equilibrium.
erqs.answer: Principle of moments: Sum of clockwise moments about a pivot equals sum of anticlockwise moments. Conditions of equilibrium: First condition ΣF = 0 (no linear acceleration); Second condition Στ = 0 (no angular acceleration).

numericals.problem:

If a small object of $0.1\text{ kg}$ is hung at any one corner from the bottom of the picture frame, then explain how the addition of the small object affects the balance of these forces and the stability of the picture frame.

1. **Disturbance of Equilibrium (Unbalanced Torque):** Initially, the picture frame is in static equilibrium because its centre of gravity lies vertically below the single suspension point. numericals.problem: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at the 50 cm mark. A 4 N weight hangs at the 20 cm mark. Where should a 6 N weight be suspended to balance the rule horizontally?
numericals.solution: Anticlockwise moment = 4 N × (50 - 20) cm = 120 N·cm. For balance, 6 N × d₂ = 120 N·cm => d₂ = 20 cm to the right of pivot (at the 70 cm mark).

numericals.problem: If a force of $4\text{ N}$ is applied by a student on a door handle and the moment of force is $16\text{ Nm}$, then the distance of the pivot from the point of applied force is
numericals.solution: From $\tau = F \times d$, the moment arm (perpendicular distance from the pivot) is $d = \frac{\tau}{F} = \frac{16\text{ Nm}}{4\text{ N}} = 4\text{ m}$.

numericals.problem: If a force of $10\text{ N}$ is acting on a body along the x-axis, then the value of this force acting on the y-axis will be
numericals.solution: A force acting purely along the x-axis has no component along the perpendicular y-axis ($F_y = F \sin(0^{\circ}) = 0\text{ N}$).
